11.0.s.en: 1. The appearance of the son of Jesse:

11.0.0.en: 1 And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots. In chapter nine he spoke of the Savior as the wonderful Child that is born: "For unto us a child is born... and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father" (Isa 9:6). Here, however, he affirms His humanity, as the King who is the son of Jesse: "And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots" [1]. He did not say the son of David, although by the Law He is the son of David, but he wished to present Him in a very humble form, as a rod and a branch of Jesse, who lived and died of little account. And the wonder is that the offspring of King David became so weak that Joseph and St. Mary came to be extremely poor.

11.0.1.en: While the inspired text in the previous chapter speaks of Assyria, who represents the enemy of the Church, as lofty and strong branches (Isa 10:33), the Messiah appears as a humble rod or branch. He wanted to crush pride, the destroyer of mankind, by His humility. As the Church says of Him on Good Friday: "He showed through weakness (the Cross) what is greater than power."

11.0.2.en: * This is Christ, who was conceived by the power of God through the Virgin of the seed of Jacob, the father of Judah and the father of the Jews, of the seed of Jesse...

11.1.s.en: 2. The Savior and the Spirit of the Lord:

11.1.0.en: "And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord." [2].

11.1.1.en: When the Lord Christ came representing humanity, the Holy Spirit rested upon Him, who is not a stranger to Him, for He is His Spirit. The resting of the Holy Spirit upon Christ differs from His resting upon us; for Him it is a hypostatic indwelling, one with Him in the same essence with the Father, an indwelling without limit. For us, however, it is a free gift and a grace granted to us in Christ Jesus as far as our nature can bear, that He may work its continual renewal. Therefore it was said of the Lord Christ that "it pleased the Father that in him should all fulness dwell" (Col 1:19; 2:9), and out of His fulness, which fills all, all believers receive grace for grace (Jn 1:16).

11.1.2.en: The Word of God is wisdom itself, and understanding and might... So the resting of the Holy Spirit is not a temporal indwelling but an eternal union among the three hypostases. In the divine Incarnation our Lord Jesus accepted the appearance of the Holy Spirit resting upon Him, in order to give to us in Him, as members of His body, the gift of the Holy Spirit, the Giver of wisdom, understanding, counsel, might, knowledge and the fear of the Lord.

11.1.3.en: Perhaps some will ask: why did the Holy Spirit rest upon the Lord Christ at His baptism? We answer: the Holy Spirit is the One who formed the humanity of the Lord Christ from the moment of the Annunciation of the divine Incarnation. And since the divinity of the Lord never parted from His humanity, His humanity was never apart from the Holy Spirit, nor in need of the Spirit's renewal for it, for it never fell into sin, nor did the old man have any place in it. Rather the Lord asked to be baptized "to fulfil all righteousness," that is, to present to us a new righteousness that we carry within us through His holy body. The resting of the Spirit upon Him was in truth for the sake of the humanity that is sanctified in Him, and so receives His Holy Spirit.

11.1.4.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa says in this: [Today (Jesus) was baptized by John, to show the one who had been defiled, and to make the Spirit descend from above, and so lift man to heaven, and raise up the fallen one who had descended and had come into shame. Christ set right all evils, taking on the whole of humanity that He might save humanity, and become an example for each one of us. Therefore He sanctifies the firstfruits and the fruits of every work He does, that He may leave to His servants a good zeal, without doubt, to follow in His steps.]

11.1.5.en: St. Gregory of Nazianzus speaks of the work of the Holy Spirit in our life as the fountain of our goodness, saying:

11.1.6.en: [He is called the Spirit of God and the Spirit of Christ... and He Himself is the Lord.

11.1.7.en: The Spirit of prophecy, of truth and of freedom, the Spirit of wisdom, understanding, counsel, might, knowledge, goodness and the fear of God.

11.1.8.en: He is the maker of all these things, He fills all by His essence and contains all things; He fills the world in His essence and yet the world cannot comprehend His power.

11.1.9.en: Good and upright, royal by nature and not by adoption.

11.1.10.en: He sanctifies and is not sanctified, He measures and is not measured, He gives participation and does not need participation, He fills and is not filled, He contains and is not contained, He bestows inheritance and glorifies... with the Father and the Son.

11.1.11.en: He is the finger of God, fire like God (the Father)...

11.1.12.en: The creating Spirit who creates anew by Baptism and the Resurrection.

11.1.13.en: He is the Spirit who knows all things, who gives where He wills, who guides, speaks, sends, sets apart and is grieved, who reveals, enlightens and gives life, or rather who is Himself the light and the life.

11.1.14.en: He creates temples and deifies (gives participation with God), He gives perfection even before baptism [as in the case of Cornelius (Acts 10:9)], and you seek Him after baptism as a gift... He works in us the divine work, He is divided into tongues of fire, distributing the gifts, He appoints apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors and teachers.

11.1.15.en: He is understood in many ways, He is clear, and He pricks the hearts...].

11.2.0.en: "And his delight shall be in the fear of the Lord: and he shall not judge after the sight of his eyes, neither decide after the hearing of his ears: but with righteousness shall he judge the poor, and rule with equity for the meek of the earth: and he shall smite the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips shall he slay the hypocrite." [3-4].

11.2.1.en: A. The Lord Christ presents to us a living picture of dealing with others: that it should not rest on bare outward appearances, and that our senses should not be the judge, especially smell, sight and hearing.

11.2.2.en: He says, "His delight His breath shall be in the fear of the Lord" [3]. The sense of smell is the quickest sense in man's life, and it must be absorbed, together with the rest of the senses, by the fear of God. Here we must distinguish three kinds of fear: the fear of slaves, the fear of hired servants, and the fear of sons. Slaves fear their masters lest they kill them, hired servants fear their employers lest they deprive them of wages or reward, but sons fear lest they wound the feelings of their fathers. This exalted fear, which the Spirit of the Lord gives us that we may revere God, is not fear of punishment or of losing the reward, but because we are sons who do not want to wound the feelings of His love.

11.2.3.en: B. "He shall not judge after the sight of his eyes" [3], but according to inner works, as the One who searches the hearts and knows the thoughts and intentions. The Lord Christ takes a stand opposed to what happened in the days of Isaiah, when the judges judged according to faces. This plague of "partiality" often strikes those who bear leadership responsibilities, and the Lord stood firmly against this pestilence, rebuking the religious leaders who were struck with partiality and hypocrisy, such as the Pharisees, the Sadducees and the scribes, while He gently called the children to Him and was merciful to sinners and tax collectors.

11.2.4.en: C. Rejection of human slanders: "neither decide after the hearing of his ears" [3].

11.3.0.en: D. His care for the poor, the wretched and the oppressed [4].

11.3.1.en: E. "And he shall smite the earth with the rod of his mouth" [4]. The Lord of glory came to smite with His word (the rod of His mouth), or with the sword of His mouth (Rev 2:16; 19:6), the two-edged sword of the Word (Heb 4:3), everyone who clung to the love of earthly things and became earth. His aim is to shatter in us the love of temporal things, in order to lift all our powers toward heavenly things.

11.3.2.en: He came to slay hypocrisy and pretense by His Holy Spirit (the breath of His lips), so that believers may live by the Holy Spirit working within them, without being occupied with deceptive appearances.

11.4.0.en: F. "And righteousness shall be the girdle of his loins, and faithfulness the girdle of his reins" [5]. The rich in the East wore a girdle embroidered with threads of gold as an ornament, a sign of greatness and splendor, and to gather up the loose robe. The poor, especially slaves, wore a cheap girdle that helps a person move quickly in serving his master and guests; the girdle was also used on journeys to gather up the garments, and soldiers used it... In any case, our Lord Jesus Christ came into the world as a spiritual King girded with righteousness and faithfulness, a sign of His wealth and beauty as the Holy One who gives the holy life, and He came as a servant girding Himself to wash human feet, so as to cleanse everyone who comes to Him.

11.4.1.en: Righteousness is often likened to a garment or a girdle, for by the righteousness of Christ we are covered and set in motion for work and striving (Job 29:14; Ps 109:18-19; Eph 6:13-17; Rev 19:8).

11.5.s.en: 4. The marks of the Messianic age:

11.5.0.en: 5 And righteousness shall be the girdle of his loins, and faithfulness the girdle of his reins. 6 The wolf also shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the kid; and the calf and the young lion and the fatling together; and a little child shall lead them. 7 And the cow and the bear shall feed; their young ones shall lie down together: and the lion shall eat straw like the ox. 8 And the sucking child shall play on the hole of the asp, and the weaned child shall put his hand on the cockatrice' den. 9 They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain: for the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the Lord, as the waters cover the sea.

11.5.1.en: After speaking of the work of the Lord Christ, he went on to speak of the Messianic age, presenting to us a living picture of it, the most striking feature of which is that believing humanity is marked by being united together in one body, bearing the nature of love and peace, so that every rebellion or violence, every love of bloodshed and killing, or of sabotage and destruction, disappears from their life.

11.6.0.en: "The wolf also shall dwell with the lamb" [6]; there is no greater contrast than this: the shedder of blood dwells with the gentle lamb, unable to defend itself. The one with the heart of a wolf, who loves to prey, lives with the person as gentle as a lamb; both bear a new nature whose constitution is love and harmony. The one who was a wolf no longer threatens the lamb, nor does the lamb fear the one who was formerly of the class of wolves, for all have become one flock bearing the new creation that is in Christ Jesus.

11.6.1.en: "And the leopard shall lie down with the kid" [6]. The first is an animal that lies in wait for its prey to attack it treacherously, and the second plays carelessly and so provokes the leopard to pounce on it... But the nature of violence and predation has been removed from the leopard, so that it lies down with the kid.

11.7.0.en: "And the calf and the young lion and the fatling together; and a little child shall lead them" [7]. A strange, mixed flock under strange leadership. Who can imagine a little boy leading a calf, accompanied by a young lion and a fatling! This little boy points to the spiritual leaders of the Church, who by a spirit of simplicity are able, by the Spirit of the Lord, to make of believers who come from different nations and peoples, and who bear varied gifts, a gentle flock that submits to the spirit of the Gospel as to a little child.

11.7.1.en: Truly gentle leaders, like the child, who know no love of domination, know how to turn lion cubs into flocks, and this by the work of the Spirit of the Lord.

11.7.2.en: "And the cow and the bear shall feed" [7]. St. Clement of Alexandria sees that the cow points to the Jews, because it is one of the animals under the yoke and is clean according to the Law, while the bear points to the Gentiles and the pagan peoples, since it is a beast of prey (violent) and unclean according to the Law. It is as though it is one of the marks of the Messianic age that members of Jewish origin come together with others of Gentile origin in one "flock," under the leadership of the one good Shepherd.

11.7.3.en: Although the bear is marked by predation, it is slow in movement, so that the milch cow counts as a precious and easy prey which it is able to devour without its escaping, unlike the young bull. Yet despite this temptation we find a strange reconciliation and friendship between them, as between their young, for it is said: "their young ones shall lie down together" [7]. This is what actually happened, for the generations that followed in the Church of the New Testament bore no distinction between those of Jewish and those of Gentile origin.

11.7.4.en: "And the lion shall eat straw like the ox" [7], for it lost its savage nature and its nature changed, so that it became like a tame animal that seeks not flesh but straw.

11.8.0.en: "And the sucking child shall play on the hole of the asp" [8]; the sucking child is no longer alarmed, because the poison of the asp has been made void.

11.8.1.en: "And the weaned child shall put his hand on the cockatrice' den" [8]. The weaned child puts his hand into the mouth of the viper and is not harmed at all.

11.9.0.en: In brief, the work of the Lord Christ is to change fierce human nature through His servants, who are marked by a spirit of gentleness, so that the whole Church, servants and those served, bears a spirit of love and unity. Thus corruption does not strike the Church, the holy mountain of the Lord, "for the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the Lord" [9], not a purely philosophical, rationalistic knowledge, but the knowledge of encounter and union and the practical experience of the new life in the Lord. This spiritual knowledge fills the life of believers as a natural matter, realized by the Incarnation of the Word of the Lord, who came to make the truth known to us, and by the work of His Holy Spirit, so that knowledge came to fill the earth "as the waters cover the sea" [9]. The Lord of glory Himself says: "It is written in the prophets, And they shall be all taught of God" (Jn 6:45; Isa 54:13; Jer 31:34; Mic 4:2; Heb 8:10; 10:16).

11.9.1.en: St. Macarius the Great speaks to us of this practical spiritual knowledge, saying: [When (the soul) is united with the Comforter Spirit in an indescribable intimacy, and is wholly mingled with the Spirit, it is counted worthy to become itself spirit; by being mingled with Him it then becomes wholly light, wholly eye, wholly spirit, wholly joy, wholly rest, wholly gladness, wholly love, wholly compassion, wholly goodness and tender mercies.]

11.10.0.en: 10 And in that day there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the Gentiles seek: and his rest shall be glorious. 11 And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, which shall be left, from Assyria, and from Egypt, and from Pathros, and from Cush, and from Elam, and from Shinar, and from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea. 12 And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth. 13 The envy also of Ephraim shall depart, and the adversaries of Judah shall be cut off: Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not vex Ephraim. 14 But they shall fly upon the shoulders of the Philistines toward the west; they shall spoil them of the east together: they shall lay their hand upon Edom and Moab; and the children of Ammon shall obey them. 15 And the Lord shall utterly destroy the tongue of the Egyptian sea; and with his mighty wind shall he shake his hand over the river, and shall smite it in the seven streams, and make men go over dryshod. 16 And there shall be an highway for the remnant of his people, which shall be left, from Assyria; like as it was to Israel in the day that he came up out of the land of Egypt.

11.10.1.en: A. The Lord Christ came to establish His Kingdom from all the nations and peoples, giving peace to the true believers: "And in that day there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the Gentiles seek: and his rest shall be glorious" [10]. The Apostle Paul quoted this prophecy when he spoke of the Gentiles glorifying God for His mercy upon them (Rom 15:6, 12), showing that his phrase "in that day" was fulfilled by the coming of the Messiah, who gathered the Gentiles into His Kingdom. The Lord of glory Jesus became an "ensign" around which the children of God that were scattered abroad are gathered together in one (Jn 11:52), so that they became one flock under one Shepherd. The Lord became an ensign proclaiming divine love in its deepest form, by being lifted up on the Cross, spreading out His hands to gather the whole world into His embrace (Jn 12:32), preaching the joy of the Gospel of salvation, which restored to man his first dignity and his victory over the powers of darkness, opening to them the gates of Paradise.

11.10.2.en: He says, "to it shall the Gentiles seek"; He is the desire of the nations, the Greeks sought Him (Jn 12:20-21); and the centurion Cornelius the Gentile sent to Peter to hear about the Lord Christ (Acts 10).

11.10.3.en: "And his rest shall be glorious"; the Jesuit translation has "his dwelling place shall be glory"; perhaps he means that His Cross, which was a shame, became glory through His Resurrection, for His empty tomb became holy to the believers, in which they perceive the truth of their Christ, the Giver of life and resurrection.

11.11.0.en: B. The Lord Christ gathers into His Church the remnant that accepted salvation, which came from scattered places (Acts 2; Jas 1:1; 1 Pet 1:1); therefore the prophet says: "And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, which shall be left, from Assyria, and from Egypt, and from Pathros (Upper Egypt), and from Cush, and from Elam (a kingdom east of the Tigris and northeast of the Persian Gulf), and from Shinar (the plain of Babylon), and from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea" [11]. This prophecy was fulfilled on the day of Pentecost, and also during the ministry of the Apostles and through the generations, and it will be fulfilled again more widely in the last days, when the Jews accept faith in the Lord Christ, as the Apostle Paul says (Rom 11:11-27). On that day those who accept the faith, coming from the Jews, join the Church that had already gathered the Gentiles, and all become members of one body: "And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth" [12].

11.11.1.en: Some interpreters try to reckon this a glory for the nation of Israel in a literal way, but here is a proclamation of the glory of the Church, which gathers from the Gentiles and the Jews together, collecting all from the ends of the world to its ends without distinction of race... for all become one Church bearing the ensign of their one Christ.

11.12.0.en: C. The union that took place between Israel (Ephraim) and Judah at their return from the captivity, after conflicts and even enmity between them had been entrenched for long centuries, presents a picture of the union between the Gentiles and the Jews [13].

11.13.0.en: In ancient times the Philistines, the people of the East, Edom, Ammon, Moab and Egypt were opposed to the people, so God gave His people the possibility of victory over them [14-16]. In the New Testament, however, the victory is not by military triumphs but by these nations accepting living faith, so that they become instruments of building and not of resistance and destruction. God, who earlier turned the sea for the salvation of His people, when He brought them across it after opening a way for them to pass through, likewise dries up all resistance in the hearts of the Gentiles, so that the way of the Messianic Kingdom is opened.

11.14.0.en: In other words, He who brought His people up from Egypt, taking them through the midst of the waters of the Red Sea, is the One who brings them across from Assyria after the captivity [16], and He is the One who brings the Gentiles across into His Kingdom despite all the obstacles and difficulties that stand before them.
